newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-EDBERG GOES DOWN SWINGING IN GRAND SLAM FAREWELL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG GOES DOWN SWINGING IN GRAND SLAM FAREWELL.

text.p: Stefan Edberg bowed out of Grand Slam tennis on Thursday, but not without a fight, taking fourth seed Goran Ivanisevic to 11-9 in a final-set tiebreaker in their U.S. Open quarter-final match.
Edberg saved four match points -- three in the tiebreak -- before falling 6-3 6-4 7-6 to end his glorious Grand Slam career.

The 30-year-old Swede, who eliminated Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands in the first round to launch a lively farewell run, ended his 54th successive Grand Slam tournament with a remarkable 177-47 record that includes six major crowns.
"I think everybody has his time. This is my 15th year on the circuit and I think I've played long enough," Edberg said in a post-match ceremony on Stadium Court.
"I've had some great years. I'll remember those."
Edberg was given a crystal plaque with his name inscribed and the image of the unisphere, the symbol of the 1964 World's Fair held here at Flushing Meadows park.

Fans will remember the image of an elegant, stylish serve- and-volley master who won the 1991 Open with devastating ease and then followed with a gritty 1992 defence when he won three successive five-set matches before reclaiming his crown.

"It is a special atmosphere when people get into the match here, all the noise and everything," said Edberg. "I think that is what I will miss about it. Being out on that court and having the crowd behind you and pushing you to the limit."
The way the crowd was pulling for Edberg, Ivanisevic said the atmosphere reminded him of playing Sweden in Davis Cup.
"It is sad because such a big player, such a champion, is leaving tennis," said Ivanisevic, who advanced to a semifinals showdown against top-seeded defending champion Pete Sampras.
"He is one of the best players ever to step on the tennis court, a big gentleman. I knew it was going to be tough today and somebody had to beat him."
The big-serving Croat cranked out 26 aces to overpower the Swede.
"I thought I came in tonight with a chance, but Goran played some really great tennis," said Edberg. "He nearly served me off the court."

With the crowd roaring him on, Edberg showed his grit in the last set. He was serving down 3-5 when he saved his first match point with a crisp backhand volley winner and then broke Ivanisevic's serve at 15-40 to even the set at 5-5 and force a tiebreak.
Three more times the blond-haired Swede thwarted Ivanisevic on match points until Edberg at last capitulated when a backhand volley off his shoe tops found the net.
"It would have been a lot harder I think going out in the first week and not really having a chance," said Edberg, ever the competitor.
"But I feel quite good right now. I feel quite relaxed, to tell you the truth."
